questions.question: What is the main objective of Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBMA), 2003?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To reduce fiscal deficit**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The main objective of the **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBMA), 2003** is to **reduce the fiscal deficit** of the government.
 
• The act aims to ensure inter-generational equity in fiscal management and long-term macroeconomic stability.
 
• It provides a legal institutional framework for reducing the fiscal deficit and improving fiscal discipline.
 
• FRBMA mandates the government to present to the Parliament a medium-term fiscal policy statement, a fiscal policy strategy statement, and a macro-economic framework statement annually along with the budget.
 
• The act also sets targets for reducing government debt and maintaining prudent levels of public spending and borrowing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The FRBMA was enacted by the Parliament of India in August 2003.
 
• The act was amended in 2018 to replace the fiscal deficit targets with a fiscal roadmap and to introduce a debt-to-GDP ratio target.
 
• According to the act, the central government is required to limit the fiscal deficit to 3% of GDP by the end of a specified period.
 
• The act also aims to eliminate revenue deficit and bring down the public debt-to-GDP ratio to a sustainable level over the medium term.
 
• Effective implementation of the FRBMA is crucial for achieving fiscal consolidation and enhancing the credibility of the government's fiscal policy.

questions.question: Orographic rainfall occurs when _____________.

options.text: the air masses collide at Intertropical Conversion Zone
hot air rises up in conventional currents
saturated air mass comes across a mountain

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**saturated air mass comes across a mountain**__

• Orographic rainfall occurs when a **saturated air mass comes across a mountain**.
 
• This type of rainfall is caused by the upliftment of moist air over a mountain barrier.
 
• As the air ascends the mountain, it cools and condenses to form clouds, leading to precipitation on the windward side

questions.question: The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948 mainly categorised the large-scale industries into __________ fragments.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**four**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 categorized large-scale industries into **four** main fragments.
 
• This policy was the first comprehensive industrial policy statement by the Government of India, aiming to lay down the pattern of industrial development.
 
• The four categories were: industries with exclusive state monopoly, basic and strategic industries, industries requiring regulation and control, and other industries.
 
• This categorization was intended to balance the roles of the public and private sectors in the industrial development of the country.
 
• The resolution was a significant step in outlining the government's approach to industrial development in post-independence India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948 aimed to promote a mixed economy where both public and private sectors would work together to achieve balanced industrial growth.
 
• It laid the foundation for subsequent industrial policies and was instrumental in shaping India's economic structure.
 
• The resolution also emphasized the importance of protecting small-scale industries and ensuring fair competition.
 
• It was followed by the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956, which further elaborated on the role of the public sector in industrial development.
 
• This policy framework was crucial in guiding India's industrial strategy during the early years of independence.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are INCORRECT vis-à-vis features of the Indian Constitution?

1) The Constitution empowers the Prime Minister to proclaim three types of emergencies.

2) A reservation policy is there to uplift the disadvantaged sections of society.

3) The Supreme Court has no power of judicial review.

4) The Constitution provides for universal adult suffrage.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 and 3**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Constitution of India does not empower the Prime Minister to proclaim emergencies; this power lies with the President of India.
 
• The Supreme Court of India does have the power of judicial review, allowing it to strike down laws that violate the Constitution.
 
• The reservation policy is indeed a feature of the Indian Constitution aimed at uplifting disadvantaged sections of society.
 
• The Constitution provides for universal adult suffrage, granting the right to vote to all citizens aged 18 and above.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November 1949 and came into effect on 26th January 1950.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the Union, State, and Concurrent lists.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in Article 368.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: 'Chhau' is a popular dance of which of the following state?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Chhau** is a traditional dance form originating from the state of **Jharkhand**.
 
• It is also popular in the neighboring states of **West Bengal** and **Odisha**.
 
• The dance is characterized by its vibrant costumes, elaborate masks, and vigorous movements.
 
• Chhau dance is traditionally performed during festivals and special occasions, often depicting stories from Indian epics like the **Mahabharata** and **Ramayana**.
 
• There are three main styles of Chhau dance: **Seraikella Chhau**, **Mayurbhanj Chhau**, and **Purulia Chhau**, each named after the region where it is performed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **UNESCO** has inscribed Chhau dance in the **Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity**.
 
• Chhau dance combines elements of martial arts, acrobatics, and athletics, making it a unique and dynamic form of artistic expression.
 
• The masks used in Chhau dance are crafted by skilled artisans and are integral to the dance, representing various characters and deities.
 
• Chhau dance is often accompanied by traditional music played on instruments like the **dhol**, **dhumsa**, and **shehnai**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the festival of Kerala that heralds the harvest season, lasts for 10 days, and has snake boat races etc?

__
 
• **Onam** is the festival of Kerala that heralds the harvest season.
 
• The festival lasts for **10 days** and is celebrated with various activities such as **snake boat races**, traditional dances, and elaborate feasts.
 
• Onam is celebrated to commemorate the homecoming of the legendary King Mahabali.
 
• It is one of the most significant festivals in Kerala and is marked by a spirit of unity and joy among the people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Onam is typically celebrated in the month of **Chingam**, the first month of the Malayalam calendar, which usually falls in **August or September**.
 
• The festival features **Pookalam** (floral decorations), **Onasadya** (a grand feast), and various cultural programs.
 
• Onam is a time when people from all communities come together to celebrate the rich cultural heritage of Kerala.
 
• The traditional attire for Onam includes the **Kasaragod saree** for women and the **Mundu** for men.
 
• Onam is also associated with the famous **Vallam Kali** (snake boat race), which is a major attraction during the festival.

questions.question: How do the muscle cells help in movement?

options.text: The blood flow of the cells helps in movement.
The thickness of the cell layer helps in movement.
The lining of the vessels inside help in movement.
The contraction and relaxation of these cells result in movement.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The contraction and relaxation of these cells result in movement**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 4** states that the contraction and relaxation of muscle cells result in movement.
 
• This is the correct mechanism as muscle cells, also known as muscle fibers, contract and relax to produce movement.
 
• Muscle contraction is initiated by signals from the nervous system and involves the interaction of actin and myosin filaments within the muscle cells.
 
• This process requires energy in the form of ATP, which is produced by cellular respiration.
 
• Relaxation occurs when the muscle cells stop receiving signals from the nervous system, allowing the muscle fibers to lengthen and return to their resting state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Muscle cells are specialized cells that contain protein filaments of actin and myosin that slide past one another to produce a contraction that changes both the length and the shape of the cell.
 
• There are three types of muscle tissue: skeletal, cardiac, and smooth. Each type has a specific function and structure.
 
• Skeletal muscles are responsible for voluntary movements, cardiac muscles are found in the heart and are responsible for pumping blood, and smooth muscles are found in various internal organs and help in involuntary movements such as digestion.
 
• Proper muscle function is essential for overall mobility, stability, and the performance of various bodily functions.

questions.question: In July 2021, which state government passed a resolution supporting an ad hoc committee report that favoured the creation of a legislative council?
questions.solution:

__
 
• In July 2021, the West Bengal state government passed a resolution supporting an ad hoc committee report that favoured the creation of a legislative council.
 
• Legislative councils are a form of bicameral legislature in Indian states, similar to the Rajya Sabha at the national level.
 
• These councils function as the upper house in states that choose to have a bicameral legislature, providing a forum for more detailed scrutiny of legislation.
 
• The creation of a legislative council requires a resolution passed by the state legislature and subsequent approval by the Parliament of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• West Bengal previously had a legislative council, which was abolished in 1969.
 
• As per Article 169 of the Indian Constitution, the Parliament can create or abolish a legislative council in a state if the legislative assembly of that state passes a resolution to that effect by a majority of the total membership of the assembly and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members of the assembly present and voting.
 
• Currently, a few Indian states such as Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, and Uttar Pradesh have legislative councils.
 
• The re-establishment of the legislative council in West Bengal is seen as a measure to provide more in-depth legislative review and representation.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a poverty alleviation programme in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rashtriya Ucchatar Shiksha Abhiyan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rashtriya Ucchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA)** is not a poverty alleviation programme; it is a centrally sponsored scheme aimed at providing strategic funding to higher educational institutions throughout the country.
 
• **Prime Minister Rozgar Yojana (PMRY)** is a poverty alleviation programme aimed at providing self-employment opportunities to educated unemployed youth.
 
• **Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY)** is a poverty alleviation programme aimed at providing gainful employment to the urban unemployed or underemployed through self-employment or wage employment.
 
• **Integrated Rural Development Program (IRDP)** is a poverty alleviation programme aimed at providing opportunities for self-employment to the rural poor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Rashtriya Ucchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA)** was launched in 2013 and aims to improve the overall quality of existing state higher educational institutions by ensuring their conformity to prescribed norms and standards.
 
• The **Prime Minister Rozgar Yojana (PMRY)** was launched in 1993 to provide sustainable self-employment opportunities to a million educated unemployed youth in the country.
 
• The **Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY)** was launched in 1997 by the Government of India to address urban poverty through gainful employment.
 
• The **Integrated Rural Development Program (IRDP)** was launched in 1978 and aimed at providing assistance to the rural poor in the form of subsidies and bank credit for productive employment opportunities.

questions.question: Article 20 of the Constitution of India is related to _____.

options.text: protection in respect of conviction for offenses
equality of opportunities in matters of public employment

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**protection in respect of conviction for offenses**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 20** of the Constitution of India provides protection in respect of conviction for offenses.
 
• This article ensures certain protections against arbitrary and unjust prosecution and punishment.
 
• It includes **protection against ex post facto laws**, which means an individual cannot be convicted of an act that was not a crime at the time it was committed.
 
• It also protects against double jeopardy, meaning a person cannot be prosecuted and punished for the same offense more than once.
 
• Additionally, it provides protection against self-incrimination, ensuring that no person accused of any offense shall be compelled to be a witness against himself.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 20** is a fundamental right enshrined in Part III of the Constitution of India.
 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
